claims.statement: Prioritize influence in the slice because command tokens fund the faction's many activations, deployments, and fleet capacity; a low-influence/high-resource slice is a more serious constraint than the converse.
claims.conditions: Draft/map dependent; the speakers prefer influence but say a 0/8 resources/influence slice is workable because Elysium can fund spending.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 458, published 2026-05-27; guide mixes Prophecy of Kings-era advice and Thunders Edge-era discussion; not independently rules-verified.
claims.uncertainty: Transcript misrecognizes several game terms; preference is strategic opinion, not a universal map rule.

claims.statement: Sell Terraform early when cash or an alliance changes the opening: the speakers set about three trade goods as a starting ask, adjust for the buyer, and value immediate money for technology, a Warfare build, or scoring above speculative later value.
claims.conditions: Raise the price when an attachment objective or four-of-a-kind objective is visible; waiting can increase value, so price it against the table and the round-one need.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 458 (2026-05-27); strategy discussion spans POK and Thunders Edge context; rules and current objective set not checked.
claims.uncertainty: The three-trade-good baseline is one speaker's negotiating heuristic; quotes vary with table wealth and buyer.

claims.statement: Consider trading Terraform for Research Agreement with Jol-Nar when the exchange gives Titans useful technology and Jol-Nar values the planet upgrade; Hyper Metabolism is singled out as attractive to Titans.
claims.conditions: Only when the tech choice, timing, and mutual value are clear; the speakers call this one of the few swaps that can beat an early cash sale.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 458 (2026-05-27), mixed-era strategic opinion; no current rules validation.
claims.uncertainty: ASR renders some faction/tech names inconsistently; component ID for the named tech is unresolved in the assigned evidence, so no ID is asserted.

claims.statement: Use scan-link to explore only a planet where a Titans unit is already present when the system is activated; it yields one planet per activation, not every planet in a multi-planet system.
claims.conditions: Pre-position a ship, Hel-Titan, or other qualifying unit on the planet before activating; do not count on a newly moved unit or sleeper placement to meet the prerequisite.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 458 (2026-05-27), guide explanation; game-rule legality was not independently checked.
claims.uncertainty: The audio/ASR calls it Scan Link / scan-link; source passage is clear about the existing-unit and one-planet constraints.

claims.statement: Treat the activation sequence as separate timing windows: scan-link exploration happens on activation, Terragenesis can then place or move a sleeper after exploring, and Awaken can redeem only a sleeper already in the activated system before that activation.
claims.conditions: Plan to explore/place now and Awaken on a later activation; a sleeper placed during the current activation cannot be redeemed by Awaken in that same action.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 458 (2026-05-27); rules explanation in the guide is not an independent rules audit.
claims.uncertainty: The speakers emphasize that wording is confusing; follow-up rules confirmation remains needed before treating as authoritative.

claims.statement: Leave sleepers unredeemed when the threat of later Awaken/coalescence is more useful than an immediate Hel-Titan: opponents can see the token and must account for the possibility of Titans entering later.
claims.conditions: Useful when preserving command tokens and creating deterrence or projection; limited by the five-token supply and opponents' willingness to avoid or challenge the location.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 458 (2026-05-27); advice draws on a reported 2023 tournament game and POK-era faction play.
claims.uncertainty: The discussion calls an unredeemed token nearly as useful, not strictly equivalent to a PDS; outcome depends on opponent behavior.

claims.statement: Use coalescence as a projection and negotiation tool: when another player enters a sleeper location, Titans can awaken into the contested area and their units participate in the ensuing combat; the speakers now regard this as a central Titans skill.
claims.conditions: Position sleepers where future access matters and budget for combat; do not treat dormant tokens as secret or as guaranteed ownership.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 458 (2026-05-27), POK-era mechanic discussion; independent legality not checked.
claims.uncertainty: The speakers revise an older dismissive view and report the tactic's use becoming more common; their assessment is experience-based.

claims.statement: Upgrade Saturn Engines early: Saturn Engine II is described as cost two, combat six, movement three, capacity two, and sustained damage, making it the core force-projection and combat upgrade.
claims.conditions: Prioritize reaching the upgrade by round two when possible; choose a route that fits available skips, breakthrough, and strategy-card timing.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 458 (2026-05-27), strategic evaluation; printed unit values and game legality not independently checked.
claims.uncertainty: Speakers use strong superlatives, but note its fleet-pool footprint and that it is not superior in every niche (for example, it lacks bombardment).

claims.statement: Treat Saturn Engine II's cheap movement and capacity as an all-purpose tool for objectives, raids, and fracture access, but account for each cruiser taking fleet capacity and for the limited number of command tokens.
claims.conditions: Best when Titans can support several fleets and enough ground forces; opponents with much greater carrier capacity or ground-force volume can exploit the all-rounder's limits.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 458 (2026-05-27), strategic synthesis across the guide; no current-rules verification.
claims.uncertainty: The speakers describe the ship as versatile rather than best-in-class at every task.

claims.statement: Spread Hel-Titans across planets to project durable ground defense and production instead of concentrating several on one planet; one per planet usually covers more ground and keeps structure objectives accessible.
claims.conditions: Multiple Hel-Titans in one system can still be useful for production; concentrate only when the objective or defense position justifies it.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 458 (2026-05-27), guide strategy opinion; current unit rules not checked.
claims.uncertainty: The source gives a general preference, not a strict threshold or universal optimum.

claims.statement: Keep at least one Hecatoncheires in reinforcements when possible, because its deploy ability converts a PDS placement into a mech plus infantry; using Transit Diodes to remove and replace a PDS can create this deployment opportunity elsewhere.
claims.conditions: Check that a mech remains in reinforcements and that the placement effect qualifies; do not fill all mech slots early if a later deployment is valuable.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 458 (2026-05-27), guide discussion of POK components and interaction; not independently rules-verified.
claims.uncertainty: The speakers call this a rules-nerdy interaction and caution that other effects that merely move ground forces do not move Hel-Titans.

claims.statement: The speakers favor spending Elysium for influence more often than its seven resources after the hero refresh, because Titans' binding shortage is command tokens rather than unit cost.
claims.conditions: Choose resources when a specific spend objective or double-tech plan warrants it; the preference assumes Saturn Engine II remains the efficient fleet backbone.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 458 (2026-05-27); hero text and economic evaluation not independently checked.
claims.uncertainty: The speakers disagree in emphasis and one calls the seven-resource use a trap; treat this as situational advice.

claims.statement: Use Tungstantus's production-triggered trade good during the same production window when it makes the build possible; Hel-Titans can generate production even when Titans otherwise lack resources.
claims.conditions: Ability requires actual production, not merely an effect that places units; spending the gained trade good immediately can also deny Mentak a later pillage opportunity per the speakers.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 458 (2026-05-27); ability/rules explanation not independently verified.
claims.uncertainty: ASR varies the commander's spelling; ID is taken from component-reference.json. The pillage timing explanation needs separate rules review.

claims.statement: Treat Terraformed Elysium as a flexible spend planet; the hero's Geoform refresh and value increase can support either influence for tokens or a large resource spend, depending on the immediate bottleneck.
claims.conditions: The discussion says Titans commonly need influence and often spend the refreshed home system for tokens, while acknowledging a seven-resource spend can enable technology or other economic goals.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 458 (2026-05-27); the recorded hero mechanic is not independently rules-checked.
claims.uncertainty: The speakers differ on which value is usually more important; do not assume one mode is always correct.

claims.statement: Use Slumber State Computing to support control-objective scoring through coexistence, including Push Boundaries; coexistence can count the planet for Titans' relevant scoring while the owner retains control, which can make the arrangement attractive to both players.
claims.conditions: Requires the breakthrough, an eligible coexistence/combat situation, and a cooperative opponent; if Titans commit no other units, the speakers say the breakthrough allows coexistence instead of ground combat.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 458 (2026-05-27), early discussion of Thunders Edge breakthrough; rules and later errata not reviewed.
claims.uncertainty: Speakers describe playtest/research games and flag uncertainty around exact interactions; preserve this as conditional advice, not settled rules.

claims.statement: Negotiate coexistence deals around concrete value: shared defense, action-card draws, a trade refresh, alliance access, objective progress, or a place to deploy structures; price benefits case by case rather than assuming the other player will agree.
claims.conditions: The speaker reports nine different deals but warns that some may have been poor value; the other player must consent to sleeper placement and may not value the exchange similarly.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 458 (2026-05-27), early playtest examples for Slumber State Computing and coalescence; not a guaranteed standard interaction.
claims.uncertainty: Anecdotes are player- and table-specific; the audio does not establish an optimal price or reliable acceptance rate.

claims.statement: Be highly cautious about enabling Yssaril to coexist for repeated action-card value; the speakers estimate the action-card flow can become very large and say a simple payment may not compensate Titans.
claims.conditions: Especially relevant early enough for multiple status phases and when the opponent can exploit or steal the extra cards; consider only with substantial trust and compensation.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 458 (2026-05-27), strategic opinion about the newly discussed breakthrough; current text not verified.
claims.uncertainty: The estimated number of cards is hypothetical; the speakers disagree only implicitly about whether any deal could justify it.

claims.statement: Value Tellurian as a flexible hit cancel: it can protect an important unit in a crucial fight, then later be used to interfere with an opponent's winning position when preserving it no longer helps Titans.
claims.conditions: Time its use around the round-two push or an endgame contest; do not assume it is the same effect as a normal sustained-damage ability.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 458 (2026-05-27), guide strategy interpretation; exact rules not independently confirmed.
claims.uncertainty: The speaker explicitly distinguishes the agent from sustained damage; situational use against an opponent is anecdotal.

claims.statement: Build toward five structures to unlock Tungstantus; sleeper placement and later Awaken can make this arrive around round two, but the speaker notes starting infantry and reachable planets may leave Titans one structure short.
claims.conditions: Count actual structures and planets reachable in the specific slice; a cooperative coexistence deal can accelerate the unlock.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 458 (2026-05-27); unlock conditions from the guide, not separately verified.
claims.uncertainty: The guide's expected timing depends on the map, infantry distribution, and deals.

claims.statement: Use the common opening plan to score a round-one public objective, then pursue Custodians if the board permits; if Titans cannot take Custodians first, the speakers prefer preserving scoring tempo and taking Imperial in round two for the bonus point.
claims.conditions: The ideal can be score plus Politics/Custodians; choose based on objective feasibility, speaker order, and whether another faction can beat Titans to Mecatol. Saar is named as a possible contest.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 458 (2026-05-27), strategic timing advice that spans POK and Thunders Edge-era game discussion; no engine verification.
claims.uncertainty: One speaker emphasizes a repeatable plan while both endorse round-one scoring over a risky Custodians-first detour; not every table position supports this.

claims.statement: Prioritize Leadership, Trade, and Politics early for tokens, money, speaker, and the round-two Imperial line; treat Technology as useful to accelerate Saturn Engine II but a middle-tier pick rather than an automatic round-one choice.
claims.conditions: Shift priorities with objectives and card order; Trade or Diplomacy can become urgent for a spend objective, and an early Warfare pop may prevent a useful Tech secondary follow.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 458 (2026-05-27), strategy-card evaluations in the guide's round-one game context; not rules-verified.
claims.uncertainty: Rankings are speaker preferences and vary with board timing; the speakers disagree on Tech urgency.

claims.statement: Use Construction only when extra opening ground forces or a specific structure/commander timing matters; Titans can often place sleepers and later turn them into multiple PDS, so they rarely need the Construction secondary.
claims.conditions: The primary may still help when the slice is ground-force constrained; the speakers give an example combining a home build with the Hecatoncheires deploy to reach more planets.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 458 (2026-05-27), guide advice; current ability timing not verified.
claims.uncertainty: Low priority is a generalization; its value rises in the described opening and objective situations.

claims.statement: A round-one Warfare primary can turn a three-planet system into rapid sleeper placement and structure progress, while creating a staging point for later expansion; Titans do not spend a command token to activate the Warfare system under the described interaction.
claims.conditions: Use when the target system and objective pattern support it; Awakening those sleepers still requires a later activation, and the guide explicitly clarifies not during that Warfare action.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 458 (2026-05-27), discussion mixes strategy-card version and faction timing; not independently rules checked.
claims.uncertainty: The value depends on the map and objective; the source says old and current Warfare both require later redemption, with perceived tempo changed by card wording.

claims.statement: Aim for Saturn Engine II by round two, using Technology primary or secondary as needed; AI Development Algorithm and an available red skip can speed the path, while green/yellow routes can support the later X-89 plan.
claims.conditions: Select based on starting skips, breakthrough availability, and strategy-card order; do not delay the unit upgrade for low-impact supplemental tech.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 458 (2026-05-27), technology recommendations; guide publication does not establish current tech legality or errata.
claims.uncertainty: The discussion leaves the exact path variable; one route through Psychoarchaeology is explicitly slice-dependent and transcript spellings vary.

claims.statement: Keep X-89 plausible as a late-game closer when Titans face opponents who can outnumber their limited-capacity cruiser fleets or overwhelm their ground defense; the speakers prefer it to Fleet Logistics in many games, while treating Fleet Logistics as still useful for an action-phase win.
claims.conditions: Make this pivot when the table's ground-force volume or scoring window justifies it; do not assume both technologies fit in the same game.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 458 (2026-05-27), strategic opinion; named technology variant and availability are not independently checked.
claims.uncertainty: The preference comes from the speaker's tournament/research games; matchup and objective dependent.

claims.statement: Treat Magen and Gravity Drive as useful supplements, and use Transit Diodes for redeployment or Hecatoncheires interactions when those effects fit; Hell-Titans cannot be moved by effects that only move ground forces according to the speakers.
claims.conditions: Magen is most valuable for holding scattered planets or control objectives; Gravity Drive helps reach the Fracture; Transit's value depends on board placement and its removal/replacement wording.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 458 (2026-05-27), strategy discussion with POK-era mechanics; not independently rules-verified.
claims.uncertainty: The transcript's 'Gamma Mama'/'Ghost Squad' names are noisy; no component IDs are assigned for those alleged counters.

claims.statement: Use the Saturn Engine II's three movement to reach the Fracture early and take relic opportunities, especially when a slice includes an ingress system that can serve as a staging or production base.
claims.conditions: The guide ranks Imperial's bonus point and public scoring ahead of fracture relics in round two; fracture access is a follow-up priority and depends on the map.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 458 (2026-05-27); Fracture advice is era-specific to the episode's Thunders Edge setting and not independently validated.
claims.uncertainty: The speakers' references to egress/ingress and relic contents are transcript-sensitive; route examples are illustrative rather than universal.

claims.statement: Exploit Titans' structure and control flexibility for stage-two objectives, including a potential Rule Distant Lands line; sleepers, Hel-Titans, and a negotiated coexistence can create positions other factions may not assemble quickly.
claims.conditions: Evaluate the revealed objective and actual control conditions; setting up a planet or a structure is preparation and does not itself score an objective.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 458 (2026-05-27), guide opinion across expansion context; no objective rules review.
claims.uncertainty: Examples are described as a dream line and option set, not guaranteed scoring; ASR and table deals affect feasibility.

connections.conditions: The token placement from Terragenesis must occur on a prior action if Awaken is to redeem that sleeper; it cannot be created and redeemed during the same activation.
A sleeper can remain dormant as a threat and be converted to a Hel-Titan when later awakened into a contested location, subject to combat.
Cruiser mobility and capacity can help Titans control enough planets; breakthrough coexistence is a separate conditional scoring avenue.
When placing a PDS on a planet with a mech available in reinforcements, the described deploy ability may substitute a mech and infantry.
Cheap mobile cruiser fleets project force, while X-89 is proposed as a way to overcome opponents' greater ground-unit volume; this is a strategic complement, not a rules dependency.
The speakers recommend using the refreshed Elysium values for influence when tokens are the constraint, preserving resources for economical cruiser builds.
Scattered Hel-Titans can make structure objectives easier to prepare for and score, subject to the objective's actual requirements.
